scope: Uganda–Kenya and Uganda–Tanzania named land crossings, plus a separate Malaba rail reference
coverage_limitations: This is a source-based reference benchmark, not a complete inventory of all physical or currently authorized border connections.
Source-verified means the named site is documented; it does not mean current operation, exact geometry or a closure-event link is verified.
Only the six core formal road sites provide a clearly bounded first benchmark; source dates and exact matching status remain separate.
not_found means no defensible association was established in this review, not that OSM contains no crossing or that extraction necessarily missed it.
Uganda and Kenya lists differ in scope; proposed, unstaffed and informal sites are retained outside the core formal-road denominator.
Lake ports and ferry routes require a separate inventory; they are not represented by all land-site records.
Opotpot is handled in the northern benchmark: the northern review found a dated NCIC report connecting it to the South Sudan border. It is not assigned to Kenya here.
Road mode for lesser-known immigration service points is provisional land-access classification where no road engineering evidence was found.
All checks are desk-based; no human field verification or independent survey was performed.

UNHCR coordinates are externally published reference positions. Their collection method, per-point observation date, accuracy and independence from OSM are undocumented; publication date is not observation date.

sources.title: Gazetted Ports of Entry and Exit (PoEs) and Location
sources.supports: Lists Suam, Lwakhakha, Malaba and Busia as active land PoEs on the Uganda border.
sources.notes: Undated webpage; active is the publisher's displayed status at retrieval, not a reconstructed operational history.

sources.title: Land PoEs
sources.supports: Identifies Busia, Malaba, Lwakhakha and Suam as road clearance points on the Kenya-Uganda border.
sources.notes: The page repeats Busia and appears to mislabel Lwakhakha county; deduplicated using the more specific immigration list.

sources.title: List of borders according to regions
sources.publisher: Uganda National Citizenship and Immigration Control
sources.supports: Lists eastern and northeastern immigration service points, including Kyebukube/Sona, Amudat, Nakabaat and Kamion; southern points include Mutukula, Kikagati and Bugango.
sources.notes: Service-point listing does not establish present staffing, legal status, exact coordinate or transport capacity. Mixed air, lake and land points; no completeness claim.

sources.title: Vote Performance Report FY2023/24 Quarter 4: Vote 120 National Citizenship and Immigration Control
sources.supports: PDF page 10 names Kamion/Oropoi, Nakabat/Lokiriama and Amudat/Alakas and reports absent immigration staffing; later pages report construction and maintenance.
sources.notes: Evidence is dated to the reporting year. Construction or an entry in a budget report is not proof of current international operation.

sources.title: Third Karamoja Integrated Development Plan 2021/22–2025/26
sources.publisher: Office of the Prime Minister, Ministry for Karamoja Affairs
sources.supports: Printed pages 27–28 distinguish Alakas as a gazetted constructed border post from Lokiriama, which the plan says required gazetting; printed page 117 lists the Alakas–Kenya road.
sources.notes: Historical planning baseline, partly citing a 2018 Government/UNDP review; legal and staffing status may subsequently have changed.

sources.title: Proposed PoEs
sources.supports: Lists Lokiriama, Konyao, Butebi and Mulwanda as proposed land PoEs on the Uganda border.
sources.notes: Proposed sites excluded from a denominator of currently operational formal crossings. Lokiriama overlaps a Ugandan reference location.

sources.title: One Stop Border Post
sources.supports: Identifies Busia, Malaba and Mutukula among Uganda's OSBPs and describes joint clearance arrangements.
sources.notes: Supports facility identity, not precise coordinates.

sources.title: Presidents Magufuli and Museveni Launch Mutukula One-Stop Border Post
sources.supports: Records the Mutukula road OSBP launch and identifies paired Busia/Busia, Malaba/Malaba and Mutukula/Mutukula sites; separately discusses earlier Malaba railway OSBP operations.
sources.notes: Road and railway references must be separated. The railway passage establishes historical existence, not current train operations.

sources.supports: Facility reference point [34.2693984,0.6327057] and Northern Corridor OSBP identity.

sources.title: Mutukula OSBP
sources.publisher: African Union Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa

sources.title: Uganda: Refugee Locations and Border Points
sources.supports: Border_Crossing worksheet rows 9, 10, 33 give Bugango, Kikagati and Mutukula names, coordinates and reported status.
sources.notes: Downloaded dataset SHA256 35087d843daf90287b90f62efed488f52c1bc204353748c60ed24fa26b013651. Its Bugango point differs by about 11 km from the OSM named-town road candidate; preserve conflict. No general Kenya-frontier inventory in this file; its Busia is in Koboko, a different location.

sources.title: Performance Audit on the Management of Invasive Alien Species in Terrestrial Environment
sources.supports: PDF page 147 / printed 130 lists Murongo, Bugango, Mtukula and Kanyigo as road entry points in Kagera.
sources.notes: PDF retrieved and read directly after web parser timeout. Audit tables use 2022 evidence. Listing does not prove every site was staffed or legally open at all later dates.

sources.title: Characterization of population connectivity for enhanced cross-border surveillance of yellow fever at Mutukula and Namanga borders in Tanzania
sources.publisher: Kakulu et al., IJID Regions; Tanzania Ministry of Health, NM-AIST and CDC research team

sources.notes: DOI 10.1016/j.ijregi.2024.100476. These are fieldwork classifications, not a legal gazette. The article itself qualifies generalizability and subjective interpretation. Indexed article text inspected; direct PMC open returned a browser check.

findings: Kenya official pages agree on four main road sites; all have plausible pilot candidates, but only Busia and Lwakhakha have supported route-level matches in this review.
Mutukula and Kikagati have published UNHCR point corroboration within about 40 m; they are the strongest eastern coordinate checks.
Bugango has a material 11 km coordinate conflict. It remains unresolved even though several official/primary sources establish the place name.
The original Mutukula major-road count includes two contacts within one facility area; these should not automatically become two crossing records.
Malaba road and rail are separate reference entities. Neither proximity of customs objects nor shared name is sufficient to transfer a truck closure to the railway.
Alakas has minor-road candidates that a primary/secondary-only inventory would omit; the post itself still requires exact localization.
Kenya proposed PoEs Konyao, Butebi and Mulwanda are documented expansion leads; not accepted as currently functioning crossings in this batch.
